_note: Coordinates verified 2026-11-13 against the cited sources; see each site's source field. lonEast is degrees east (west negative).

sites.name: Mons Mouton
sites.story: Target of Intuitive Machines IM-2 Athena (Mar 2025). It tipped over in a crater; low sun angles and long shadows were part of the cause.
sites.source: IM-2 Athena touchdown point (Intuitive Machines / LROC); Mons Mouton is a NASA Artemis III candidate region

sites.name: Near Shackleton (Chang'e-7)
sites.story: China's Chang'e-7 target: a sunlit peak on the ridge near Shackleton crater. Its Aug 2026 launch was postponed with no new date announced, which makes it a real Slip Test case.
sites.source: CNSA candidate site, as presented to UN COPUOS (Feb 2025); not NASA, not a final site

sites.name: Malapert Massif
sites.story: A tall massif facing the Earth side of the Moon. Often cited as good for direct-to-Earth communication.
sites.source: NASA Artemis III candidate region; notional landing point from Kring et al. 2025, JGR Planets, doi:10.1029/2024JE008905

sites.name: Haworth
sites.story: Plateau beside Haworth crater, whose permanently shadowed floor may hold water ice. High science value, harder power and comms.
sites.source: NASA Artemis III candidate region 'Haworth' (centre of the PGDA Haworth 5 m DEM tile)

sites.name: Chandrayaan-3 (Shiv Shakti)
sites.story: India's successful 2023 landing. Far south, but not at the pole, so the Sun climbs much higher.
sites.source: ISRO landing; position from NASA LRO LROC imaging (not a NASA mission)

sites.name: Apollo 11 (Tranquility Base)
sites.story: Equatorial site: two weeks of high sun, two weeks of night, and Earth always high in the sky.
sites.source: NASA NSSDCA Apollo landing site coordinates (LM)
